messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: P1 - gpu-node-42 (us-west-2a) kernel panic detected. Alert: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD12345 :rotating_light: Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/infrunbooks/gpu-kernel-panic

pagerduty: Alert acknowledged by sam at 2025-06-03T03:40:40Z. Responders: eng-oncall.

sam: Acked. I'm on it, pulling serial console and kubelet logs. tagging @neha @dave for visibility.

neha: Thanks. Any immediate customer impact?

dave: From alerting: kubelet reported NotReady, node marked Unschedulable by autopilot, a few tenant pods evicted. Metrics show a spike in 504s from inference-cluster on us-west-2 (~00:30 UTC) :chart_with_upwards_trend:.

sam: Serial console dump (tail):
```
[  123.456789] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
[  123.457012] CPU: 3 PID: 0 Comm: swapper Not tainted 5.10.0
[  123.457128] Call trace:
[  123.457200]  ? gpu_driver_oops+0x1a0/0x250
[  123.457345]  dump_stack_lvl+0x45/0x70
[  123.457456]  panic+0x123/0x3f0
```

neha: Ugh, looks like a GPU driver oops. NVidia stack in the trace. We should consider hardware path if node keeps panicking after reboot.

dave: Agreed. For mitigation: cordon + drain to move active pods off the node and restore capacity. We might need to re-schedule heavy jobs to other racks to avoid throttling.

sam: Running cordon/drain now. commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 -n infra
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force -n infra
```

sam: Drain completed, 6 pods evicted, 4 pods failed to reschedule immediately (pending GPU). Placing a temp capacity alert to autoscaler. :wrench:

neha: Customer impact: ticket CN-8472 (inference-saas) reports repeated 504s for certain model endpoints between 00:28-00:36 UTC. Looks correlated. I tagged support and posted a blameless note.

dave: I'll kick off placement override to allow burst into reserved pool while we triage. Putting a short-term rule: prefer-dedicated-pool for inference-critical.

sam: Attempting soft reboot via IPMI, if that fails we escalate to serial console vendor RMA. IPMI output:
```
ipmitool -H bmc-usw2 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle
Chassis Control: Reset/Power Down
```

sam: Node came back but kubelet failed to become Ready; logs show repeated kernel oops during early boot. Reboot loop observed.

neha: Escalate to hw-rma-bot/hardware team. We need manual intervention (possible PCIe/GPU hardware fault).

hw-rma-bot: RMA ticket created: RMA-9921. On-call hardware to pick up. ETA technician on site 4h.

dave: For rollout: mark node as GONE in inventory and exclude from scheduling until RMA completed. I'll add a migration plan for tenants on that rack.

sam: Handing off primary oncall to maria for continued monitoring and RMA follow-through. I will stay on the channel for context. :hand:
maria: Taking over. Thanks @sam. I'll coordinate with hardware and support, and post status updates every 30m or on significant changes. Current status summary:
- Node: gpu-node-42, us-west-2a
- Symptom: kernel panic -> reboot loop on boot, NVidia driver trace
- Customer impact: some 504s, 4 pods pending due to GPU shortage, support ticket CN-8472 opened
- Actions taken: cordon/drain, temporary placement override, reboot attempts, RMA ticket RMA-9921 opened

maria: Next steps: continue RMA, monitor autoscaler and placement rules, rotate affected pods into dedicated pool, notify customers via support. If node recovers after full power cycle and firmware re-flash, we'll run stress / repro job before returning to rotation.

sam: adding note to incident timeline and will attach kernel oops logs to RMA ticket. :page_with_curl:

maria: Acknowledged. I'll close the PagerDuty incident when hardware handoff is complete and node is removed or recovered. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident resolved by maria at 2025-06-03T08:05:00Z (RMA in progress, node removed from rotation).
